directions.question: How do open-source contributor communities regain workable alignment of interdependent activity after impairment?
directions.logical_move: P(S,C)? -> P(S-prime,C)?; substitute an organizational subject class while preserving P, C and scope.
directions.discovery_target: Whether replacement of contribution and review relationships restores aligned joint development after impairment; do not equate commit output with P.

directions.bridge_test: First establish interdependent contributions and a dated impairment of their alignment. Then test whether changes in participation, review and decision rights precede renewed compatible work against the same outcome threshold used for teams. Distinguish project-community and team boundaries; compare only episodes without coercive management.
directions.novelty_reason: Changes membership boundaries, employment relationship and control over a shared artifact; this is more than relabeling a remote team.

fixed.P: Regain a workable capacity to align interdependent activity after impairment.
fixed.C: An event or episode associated with interruption or impairment of ongoing joint activity; origin, duration and severity remain unspecified. After remains temporal, not causal.
fixed.comparison_rule: Apply the same demonstrated interdependence, impairment, and workable-alignment outcome requirements to S and S-prime. Do not substitute productivity, service delivery, resource sustainability, or survival for coordination recovery.

changed.S_prime: Voluntary, permeable contributor communities organized around a shared software artifact, rather than a bounded employment team.
changed.not_assumed: The replacement class need not have every property of decentralized teams; comparability and the non-coercion boundary require explicit checks.

directions.finding: An author-hosted study reports a productivity decrease among remaining developers after core-developer dropout. Apache documents volunteer, consensus-based project governance. These establish a plausible distinct collective and an impairment route, but neither inspected item establishes restored coordination.

candidate_validity.evidence: Class/governance and shock evidence; recovery mechanism unestablished.

unknowns: Whether sampled projects meet the volunteer and non-coercive criteria.
Whether a productivity decrease reflects coordination impairment rather than less labor.
Observed recovery trajectories and a coordination outcome threshold.
